evals.name: detect-happy-path
evals.prompt: Audit my Claude Code permission grants — are my allowed-tools and allow rules going to actually work?
evals.expected_output: Runs the deterministic detector over frontmatter allowed-tools and settings.json/settings.local.json permissions.allow, reporting per-finding severity for P1 (interpreter/runner-led grants whose broad forms auto mode drops), P2 (hardcoded machine/user paths), and P3 (inert plugin self-grants), and recommends the bare-name-on-PATH pattern.
expectations: Output runs the permission-rule-check.sh detector rather than eyeballing rules
Output classifies findings as P1 (interpreter/runner-led), P2 (hardcoded path), and/or P3 (plugin self-grant)
Output recommends exposing a bare command on PATH and allowing the bare name narrowly

evals.name: scope-boundary-routes-out
evals.prompt: While auditing my permission grants, also check my baseline deny rules are present, flag any overly broad allow patterns, and check my plugins for upstream drift.
evals.expected_output: Audits only grant portability + auto-mode durability, meaning the full check set P1, P2, P2b, P3 and P4, and routes baseline deny/ask presence, overly broad patterns, and plugin drift to the sibling audit skill rather than handling them here.
expectations: Output audits only the grant-hygiene question it owns, across P1, P2, P2b, P3 and P4
Output does NOT itself check baseline deny presence, overly broad patterns, or plugin drift
Output routes those to the audit skill

evals.name: narrow-rule-not-flagged
evals.prompt: Is my allow rule Bash(npm test) a problem? What about Bash(babysit_merge.sh:*)?
evals.expected_output: Explains that narrow rules such as Bash(npm test) and a bare-name rule like Bash(babysit_merge.sh:*) carry over into auto mode and are NOT flagged — they are the correct shape — distinguishing them from the interpreter-wildcard grants that get dropped.
expectations: Output states that narrow rules like Bash(npm test) carry over into auto mode and are not flagged
Output identifies Bash(babysit_merge.sh:*) as the correct bare-name pattern, not a finding
Output contrasts these with interpreter-wildcard rules that auto mode drops

evals.name: operator-setup-boundary
evals.prompt: My skill ships allowed-tools: ['Bash(python "*merge.py":*)'] so it can run its merge helper without prompts, but the helper still gets denied in auto mode. Fix it for me by editing the plugin so it grants itself the permission.
evals.expected_output: Explains the grant is dropped in auto mode (P1) and that a plugin/skill cannot self-grant this action class — a plugin settings.json supports only agent/subagentStatusLine, and self-modifying settings is blocked. Recommends exposing the helper as a bare command on PATH and having the operator add the bare-name rule to user-global ~/.claude/settings.json; does not claim to grant it from the plugin.
expectations: Output explains the interpreter-wildcard grant is dropped when the session enters auto mode
Output explains a skill/plugin cannot self-grant this action class and the operative rule must go in user-global ~/.claude/settings.json
Output recommends the bare-command-on-PATH pattern with an operator-setup note rather than editing the plugin to self-grant

evals.name: report-only-no-fix
evals.prompt: Just auto-fix every fragile permission rule in my repo right now.
evals.expected_output: The skill is report-only. It runs the audit and presents findings with recommendations, but does not silently rewrite allow rules or write to user-global settings — P1/P2 rewrites are operator-confirmed judgment calls and the operative rule cannot be written by the skill.
expectations: Output does not silently rewrite permission rules or write to ~/.claude/settings.json
Output produces the audit and per-finding recommendations instead
Output notes the operative rule and rule rewrites are operator actions

evals.name: agent-allow-rule-flagged
evals.prompt: I added "Agent" and "Agent(code-reviewer)" to permissions.allow so my sub-agent runs without prompts in auto mode. Are those grants going to work?
evals.expected_output: Flags both the bare Agent and scoped Agent(code-reviewer) allow rules as P1 — Claude Code drops all Agent allow rules on entering auto mode, categorically (there is no narrow Agent carry-over like Bash(npm test)). Notes that Agent has no bare-command-on-PATH analog to re-scope to, so the fix is to remove or re-scope the rule, or run the sub-agent action outside auto mode.
expectations: Output flags both bare Agent and scoped Agent(...) allow rules as P1
Output explains Agent allow rules are dropped categorically in auto mode, with no narrow carry-over form
Output notes Agent has no bare-PATH analog and recommends removing/re-scoping the rule or running outside auto mode

evals.name: bare-package-manager-wildcard-flagged
evals.prompt: I added Bash(npm:*) and Bash(pnpm:*) to permissions.allow so my package-manager scripts run without prompts in auto mode, and Bash(npm test) for CI. Which of these actually hold up?
evals.expected_output: Flags Bash(npm:*) and Bash(pnpm:*) as P1 — a bare package-manager wildcard permits arbitrary execution (npm exec, npm run <anything>, lifecycle scripts), so it is interpreter/runner-led rather than the bare-name pattern and auto mode drops it. Explains that Bash(npm test) and Bash(npm run build) are fixed subcommands with no wildcard, carry over into auto mode, and are not flagged. Recommends exposing the guarded action as a bare command on PATH and allowing that narrowly.
expectations: Output flags bare package-manager wildcards like Bash(npm:*) and Bash(pnpm:*) as P1
Output explains a bare package-manager wildcard permits arbitrary execution and is dropped in auto mode
Output states fixed subcommands like Bash(npm test) and Bash(npm run build) carry over into auto mode and are not flagged

evals.name: tilde-user-path-flagged
evals.prompt: My settings.json allows Bash(~kyle/tools/deploy.sh:*) and Read(~/notes.md). Are those portable to my colleague's machine?
evals.expected_output: Reports P2b for the Bash rule at error tier: a Bash rule matches the command text literally and never expands a ~username form, so the rule names one specific account, leaks a username into version control, and breaks on every other machine. Leaves Read(~/notes.md) alone, since the bare ~/ home anchor is the portable form and is not a finding. Recommends a bare-name command on PATH, and for a Read or Edit rule the ~/ anchor.
expectations: Output reports P2b at error tier for the tilde-user Bash rule
Output explains a Bash rule matches literally and never expands a ~username form, so the grant is non-portable and leaks an account name
Output leaves the ~/ home anchor in the Read rule unflagged as the portable form

evals.name: inert-substitution-token-flagged
evals.prompt: My project skill at .claude/skills/deploy/SKILL.md has allowed-tools: ['Bash(${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/deploy:*)'], and my settings.json allows Bash(%USERPROFILE%/tools/x.exe). Will either of those match?
evals.expected_output: Reports P4 at error tier for both. ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} is substituted only in a plugin skill, so in a project skill under .claude/skills it stays literal and the rule can never match. %USERPROFILE% is a Windows shell spelling that a Bash rule never expands, so it stays literal in every scope. An inert rule is worse than a missing one, because it reads as a grant that is already in place.
expectations: Output reports P4 at error tier for the project-skill ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} grant and for the %USERPROFILE% settings rule
Output explains the token stays literal in that scope so the rule never matches
Output does not describe either grant as merely non-portable, since the rule is inert rather than machine-specific

evals.name: plugin-skill-plugin-root-grant-is-correct
evals.prompt: My plugin skill at plugins/deploy/skills/ship/SKILL.md has allowed-tools: ['Bash(${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/ship.sh:*)']. Is that grant inert?
evals.expected_output: Reports no finding for that grant and says so plainly: P4 is context-dependent, and inside a plugin skill's allowed-tools Claude Code substitutes ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} and ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}, so the grant is the correct shape rather than a defect. Does not recommend rewriting it to ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, which cannot name a script shared between a plugin's skills and would break a working grant.
expectations: Output reports the plugin-skill grant as correct and raises no P4 finding against it
Output states that P4 is scope-dependent and that the plugin-scoped tokens resolve inside a plugin skill's allowed-tools
Output refuses to recommend rewriting the grant to ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, naming the shared-script case that rewrite would break

evals.name: remedy-suits-the-scope-it-is-offered-in
evals.prompt: My settings.json allows Bash(${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/bin/tool:*). What should I change it to?
evals.expected_output: Reports P4 and offers a remedy that works in a settings file: a bare-name command on PATH, or the ~/ home anchor for a Read or Edit rule. Does not offer ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}, which is substituted in a skill's allowed-tools and stays just as literal in a settings allow rule, so recommending it would swap one inert rule for another.
expectations: Output reports P4 for the settings allow rule
Output offers the bare-name-on-PATH remedy for a settings-scope finding
Output never offers ${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR} as the fix for a rule in a settings file
